title: Mixed report on Zirkzee for Juventus from Manchester United with €35m option
description: There are mixed reports over the status of Juventus negotiations with Manchester United for Joshua Zirkzee, on loan with an option to buy for €35m.It is no secret that the Bianconeri need at least o...
fullText:
There are mixed reports over the status of Juventus negotiations with Manchester United for Joshua Zirkzee, on loan with an option to buy for €35m.

It is no secret that the Bianconeri need at least one new striker after losing Dusan Vlahovic and with Lois Openda heading to Olympique Lyonnais.

Zirkzee has also been on their radar for a very long time, even before he made the move from Bologna to Manchester United for €42.5m in the summer of 2024.

MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – MAY 20: Joshua Zirkzee of Manchester United looks on during a Manchester United training session ahead of the UEFA Europa League Final 2025 between Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester United at Carrington Training Ground on May 20, 2025 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

Sun Sport claim today that Juventus are in ‘advanced negotiations’ to bring him to Turin on loan with an option to buy for €35m.

The reports from Sky Sport Italia are less enthusiastic about the state of talks, suggesting that this is going to be a difficult and complex process that is not close to completion.

The cost of the fee is just one issue, as his salary is also a problem for the Old Lady after failing to qualify for the Champions League.

Their first choice remains Randal Kolo Muani, so if he arrives from Paris Saint-Germain, there won’t be funds enough for both.

MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 30: Joshua Zirkzee of Manchester United looks on during the Carabao Cup Fourth Round match between Manchester United and Leicester City at Old Trafford on October 30, 2024 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images)

In two years, Zirkzee has scored nine goals and provided four assists in 75 competitive appearances for Manchester United, but never managed to get regular starts.

title: Dave Roberts Updates Shohei Ohtani’s Status Amid Knee Injury
description: Los Angeles Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani is dealing with a knee injury, and manager Dave Roberts revealed how that injury impacts his usage.
fullText:
Los Angeles Dodgers two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani continues to lead off the batting order, but he’s recently been held out of the pitching rotation due to pain in his left knee.

His progression back to the mound was recently paused, as his expected bullpen session on Saturday was canceled due to knee pain.

With Ohtani forming a core part of the anticipated starting rotation for the playoffs, questions remain about how best to handle him the rest of the regular season.

Manager Dave Roberts recently weighed in on that question and revealed his thought process behind using Ohtani when speaking with Katie Woo of The Athletic.

Though Ohtani normally pitches only once every six games as part of the starting rotation, he plays pretty much every game at designated hitter.

So does that offensive play affect his knee?

Roberts said he spoke with Ohtani about that, and the superstar said his knee pain is unrelated to hitting.

“From his words, the hitting, the running, as he has done the last couple nights, doesn’t affect him,” Roberts told Woo. “I can only go by what he and the training staff are telling me. So, unless I hear otherwise, that hitting compromises his health, then I’m going to keep putting him in the lineup.”

Woo also reported that the Dodgers won’t push Ohtani to throw another bullpen session “until he feels 100 percent” out of fears that he could get injured even more.

“Should Ohtani rush a comeback, he risks overcompensating, which could lead to other issues not as treatable as the team believes his knee is,” Woo wrote.

And if Ohtani were to get hurt in a way that prevents him from hitting as well, that could be truly disastrous for the team’s goal of a three-peat.

After all, Roberts has admitted that the Dodgers value Ohtani more as a hitter than a pitcher.

And with hurlers like Justin Wrobleski, an All-Star this season, ready to step in as a pitcher if needed, there’s no need to rush Ohtani back to the mound.

So while this knee pain could cost Ohtani a shot at a Cy Young Award this season, it keeps everyone’s ultimate goal, a World Series, in play.

title: FSU football injury report: How healthy are the Seminoles for preseason
description: Florida State football head coach Mike Norvell provided an injury update on his Seminoles team ahead of the start of preseason camp.
fullText:
Florida State football head coach Mike Norvell provided an injury update on his Seminoles team ahead of the start of preseason camp.

At his annual preseason media luncheon, Norvell said that "guys are progressing well" and that there will be some players who are "limited" to start camp.

Wide receiver Jayvan Boggs and linebacker Mikai Gbayor are both players who should get significant play time this season, but both were hurt in spring. Norvell didn't comment on when he expected them back; however, he suggested the duo could be ready to play by the opening weeks of the season.

"We'll see exactly where they are," Norvell said. "They definitely both have an open door of opportunity of being ready for the first game... We'll see how that plays out as we get closer, but I like their progress."

Among the other players who will be limited or miss preseason camp are transfer linebacker Chris Thomas, who arrived on campus with an injury to his knee, and freshman defensive lineman Cam Brooks, who suffered an Achilles injury.

The Seminoles will get a boost with talented freshman linebacker Izayia Williams and transfer defensive lineman Jordan Sanders both available at the start of camp.

"Sanders will be full, ready to go," Norvell said.

"He's fully cleared. He definitely looks the part. I'm excited to see him out at practice," Norvell added on Williams.

Liam Rooney covers Florida State athletics for the Tallahassee Democrat. Contact him via email at LRooney@gannett.com or on Twitter @__liamrooney.

This article originally appeared on Tallahassee Democrat: FSU football injury report: How healthy are the Seminoles for preseason

title: Falcons land WR help in 2027 NFL mock draft from CBS Sports
description: Falcons take 6-foot-3 Texas WR in 2027 NFL mock draft from CBS Sports
fullText:
There are some major question marks surrounding the Atlanta Falcons' roster as the team prepares to kick off training camp this week in Flowery Branch. From the starting quarterback competition to the battle for the No. 2 wide receiver job, Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski has much to figure out over the next month.

The team signed former first-round pick Jahan Dotson to replace speedster Darnell Mooney, but it's fair to question whether or not he's capable of filling that role. Dotson's career stats suggest otherwise, however, it's tough to produce when you're stuck behind two elite receivers, as he was in Philadelphia.

Former Georgia wide receiver Zachariah Branch appears to have a bright future, assuming his effectiveness isn't hindered by his lack of size. Depending on how this season goes, the Falcons may or may not be looking for a new No. 2 wide receiver in 2027.

Atlanta lands a perfect complement to Drake London in a new CBS Sports mock draft from Mike Renner. The Falcons were projected to take Texas wide receiver Cam Coleman with the sixth overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.

"Cam Coleman is a wildly explosive 6-foot-3, 200-pound wideout who spent the past two seasons stuck with poor quarterback play at Auburn," wrote Renner. "That changes this year as he heads to Texas to pair with Arch Manning. He should be a household name by season's end."

Coleman racked up 93 receptions for 1,306 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns (14.0 yards per catch) over the last two seasons at Auburn. The Falcons have dealt with similar quarterback issues over the past few years, so Coleman would feel right at home in Atlanta.

The Falcons did re-sign London to a four-year, $141 million contract extension during the offseason, however, there is still a clear lack of depth behind him. Branch could be a long-term option in the slot with No. 2 upside, but it wouldn't hurt to add to the receiver room in 2027.

For now, Atlanta is set to kick off training camp with its current wide receiver group. Although, we wouldn't be surprised to see the team add someone like Stefon Diggs or Keenan Allen before camp ends.

This article originally appeared on Falcons Wire: Falcons land WR help in 2027 NFL mock draft from CBS Sports

title: Chelsea in talks with ex-Man United and Arsenal star as Xabi Alonso eyes attack boost
description: Chelsea have reportedly opened talks with Brighton and Hove Albion over a potential transfer for veteran striker Danny Welbeck ahead of the 2026/27 Premier League season
fullText:
Chelsea have initiated discussions with Brighton and Hove Albion regarding a potential move for Danny Welbeck, according to football.london.

It has emerged that club-to-club talks have begun between the Blues and the Seagulls, with the intention of bringing the center-forward to Stamford Bridge ahead of the upcoming season.

At 35 and in the latter stages of a career which has seen him represent Manchester United and Arsenal among others, Welbeck turned back the clock with Brighton last season, netting 14 goals and contributing two assists across all competitions.

As a result, the decision-makers in West London have kicked off negotiations to secure his services ahead of 2026/27 - given last season's attacking options struggled to deliver consistent performances.

While Joao Pedro managed 15 goals and eight assists in the Premier League, Liam Delap found the back of the net just once despite making 28 appearances, raising serious questions over his suitability to the club.

Bringing Welbeck on board would ultimately strengthen Chelsea's attacking options, particularly if Xabi Alonso can unlock his best form.

Brighton declined to comment on the matter when approached for a response by football.london.

Although Chelsea may have had a sluggish start to the summer transfer window, it now appears that the club's hierarchy has begun to set things in motion. Chelsea have bolstered their squad significantly, adding Dastan Satpaev, Denner, Emmanuel Emegha, Geovany Quenda and Marco Palestra before capping their recruitment drive with the £117 million ($156.5 million) acquisition of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

Reflecting on his move via the club's official website, Rogers said: "I'm so excited. For me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I've always admired since I was a kid.

"I'm really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we've got and where the club is heading. That's why I'm here and I can't wait to get started."

"You need players who can have that almost instant impact and I'm sure Morgan won't need much time to adapt to the club, the system and his team-mates. That was the idea, to get a top player, and Morgan is one of them."

title: PSG aim dig at Real Madrid after losing Yan Diomande race: ‘This shows where they are’
description: Real Madrid had spent most of their summer transfer window placing emphasis on defensive reinforcements and not making any moves in attack.Yesterday, however, Los Blancos leapfrogged PSG and reportedl...
fullText:
Real Madrid had spent most of their summer transfer window placing emphasis on defensive reinforcements and not making any moves in attack.

Yesterday, however, Los Blancos leapfrogged PSG and reportedly reached an agreement with RB Leipzig to sign Yan Diomande for a huge fee.

The Ivory Coast international is widely regarded as one of the biggest talents in the world, and he is set to join the biggest club in the world.

Real Madrid’s pursuit of Diomande has sparked a pointed response from PSG, with the French champions explaining why they refused to match the financial demands involved in the deal.

In an unofficial statement issued via L’Equipe, PSG dismissed suggestions that they were willing to enter a bidding war for the highly rated youngster after Real Madrid moved into pole position.

PSG have fired shots at Real Madrid. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

In a strongly worded statement, PSG said: “They were asking for crazy money for a player who has potential but was playing in the Spanish second division one year ago. We won’t break the bank because a club arrived with fireworks.”

PSG then concluded with a pointed remark aimed directly at Real Madrid.

“This shows where Real Madrid are right now.”

The comments underline PSG’s frustration after missing out on one of Europe’s most promising young talents.

Real Madrid, however, have shown repeatedly in recent years that they are prepared to invest heavily when they identify a player they believe can become part of the club’s long-term core.

If Los Blancos are convinced Diomande fits that profile, criticism from a rival is unlikely to alter their strategy.

Diomande will join Real Madrid soon. (Photo by Stuart Franklin/Getty Images)

PSG have had their own share of dubious decision-making in the past, and it is quite baffling to see them throw shade because they missed out on an incredible talent.

The relationship between Real Madrid and PSG has become increasingly tense in recent years, particularly in the transfer market.

From Kylian Mbappe to emerging young talents, the two clubs have frequently found themselves competing for the same elite players.

The Diomande saga appears to be the latest chapter in that rivalry.

Ultimately, only time will determine whether Real Madrid’s investment proves justified.

If Diomande develops into the player the club believe he can become, the transfer fee will quickly be forgotten.

title: Gianni Infantino Lashes Out at World Cup Critics
description: The FIFA president ripped the media in an Instagram post.
fullText:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino posted a 15-slide message directed at people “busy planting seeds of hate” on Instagram on Sunday night, claiming the World Cup went off without incident.

Infantino’s Sunday night missive began: “To everyone who missed our beautiful game…sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all.” He went on to further single out people “behind their pens and papers, behind their screens spreading hate and false rumours.”

The post was filled with jarring and inaccurate claims; he wrote that the World Cup saw “zero incidents, zero hostility, zero violence, just joy, emotions, happiness, unity, and togetherness.”

Four people died during celebrations in Mexico City after Mexico beat Ecuador in the round of 32. South African midfielder Jayden Adams was found dead in Cape Town after returning from the tournament, and police are investigating a cause of death.

FIFA did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the inaccuracies or what prompted Infantino’s post.

Even and especially at its best, the World Cup—as always—stirred up hostility and political tensions. Argentine fans in Atlanta were captured on video fighting with one another on the night before the match, and with England fans after the semifinal win. The match reignited historic claims from the Argentine government, players, and fans against Great Britain over the Falkland Islands, including with an on-pitch demonstration by the players. In the U.K., more domestic abuse incidents were reported during the tournament than the past two World Cups and Euros.

Infantino also wrote that “Iran entered the United States without incident or conflict.” Iran’s coach, though, said his side was “perhaps the most oppressed” team in the tournament after the quick trip from Tijuana to Los Angeles took five hours with security screenings, then the team would need to return immediately after the match. Iran saw 11 federation members and team staffers denied entry into the U.S., including federation president Mehdi Taj.

The Iranian federation also said it would file a complaint to FIFA for denying its request to travel two days in advance of its match against Belgium.

Infantino wrote that “Football is bigger than hate and discrimination.” Multiple incidents of racist abuse occurred during the World Cup. Most notably, a Paraguayan senator called Kylian Mbappé a “colonised Cameroonian,” to which the French captain called her “a despicable woman and unworthy of your position.”

Infantino said the World Cup’s haters “mentioned the few people denied visas and overlooked the millions who were approved, from all parts of the world.”

The most high profile visa cases include that of Somali referee Omar Artan, denied entry into the U.S. over alleged “association with suspected members of terrorist organizations,” and Ghana midfielder Thomas Partey, who was not allowed into Canada for matches due to ongoing rape charges.

And fans from Haiti, Iran, Senegal, and Ivory Coast were simply banned from entering the United States under blanket Trump administration policy; others were subject to a $15,000 bond that deterred many from coming. (FIFA celebrated that it got the U.S. to waive this requirement, but that only applied to a certain subset of fans who had already purchased tickets and opted into an expedited visa process.)

Infantino did not mention Folarin Balogun’s red card or its subsequent suspension directly, but he was still defensive about the notorious incident.

“Indeed, ‘arguable’ referees’ decisions or ‘strange’ disciplinary rulings such as for instance potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide,” Infantino wrote. “It’s curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising.”

European leaders had blasted FIFA’s handlingof Balogun’s red card to the point where UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin—whose organization called the red card reversal an “unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable decision”—boycotted the tournament final. (Some European leagues do review red cards after games, which is not generally FIFA protocol.)

Infantino has not taken questions from reporters since a press conference before the opening match in Mexico City on June 10.

There, Infantino was also defensive and vague, saying, “We try to do our best” on a number of issues like Iran, high ticket prices, and visa restrictions. After initially telling people to “chill, relax,” Infantino later clarified that he meant “to trust us that we are working behind the scenes.”

He was more aggressive on Sunday night.

“To those spending their time and energy hating us, please take a moment to reflect, meditate, pray, or watch a football match and truly observe the faces, the eyes, the emotions,” Infantino wrote. “To the pens and papers, to all the screens, may you find love and peace where the people behind you couldn’t.

“May you find peace; we at FIFA have found ours and we deliver it, by delivering the most outstanding FIFA World Cup.”

Also on Sunday night, Rep. Jamie Raskin (D., MD) sent Infantino a letter asking for a list of any money or gifts exchanged between FIFA and anyone related to President Trump, and visitor logs at the governing body’s Miami and New York offices. FIFA houses its New York office in Trump Tower. The Athletic first reported news of the letter.

Raskin also asked Infantino to appear before the House Judiciary Committee, of which he is the ranking member.

The post Gianni Infantino Lashes Out at World Cup Critics appeared first on Front Office Sports.

title: Crystal Palace move on €30m defender deal
description: Crystal Palace Closing In on Chrislain Matsima as Augsburg Talks Reach Final StageCrystal Palace appear to be moving closer to a significant summer addition, with fresh movement reported in the club��...
fullText:
Crystal Palace appear to be moving closer to a significant summer addition, with fresh movement reported in the club’s pursuit of Chrislain Matsima. According to Florian Plettenberg, “New negotiations took place today between Crystal Palace and FC Augsburg for Chrislain Matsima.” That update alone suggests Palace are working hard to get this one over the line as they continue shaping their squad for the season ahead.

The latest position points to a deal that is advanced, even if it has not yet crossed the finish line. Plettenberg states, “Matsima is still in Augsburg. He has not yet been given the green light to travel for his medical.” That detail matters, because it underlines that while confidence may be growing, the formal final steps are still being negotiated.

There is clearly encouragement around the transfer. As reported, “It‘s advanced.” Palace and Augsburg are now said to be focusing on the finer points, with “the clubs are discussing the final details, including the payment structure and bonuses.” For any deal of this size, those final conversations can often prove decisive, especially when performance-related clauses and instalment terms become central to negotiations.

The financial scale of the move also stands out. The report adds, “The total package is expected to exceed €30 million once the deal is completed.” That would represent a major commitment from Crystal Palace and a clear sign of intent in the market. Matsima is a player Palace seem prepared to back heavily, which hints at the level of belief behind the scenes.

For now, one final hurdle remains. Plettenberg notes that “The final green light from both clubs is still pending but could arrive soon.” Palace supporters will take plenty of encouragement from that line, because it paints this transfer as one that is very much alive and edging towards completion.

From a hopeful Crystal Palace fan perspective, this feels like the kind of move that can really lift the mood. If the club are ready to go beyond €30 million for Chrislain Matsima, then it suggests they see real quality, real upside and a player who can become important very quickly. That is exactly the sort of ambition supporters want to see.

What stands out most is the phrase, “It‘s advanced.” Those two words are enough to get fans excited, especially when the rest of the update points to a deal that is now about structure rather than principle. If payment terms and bonuses are the main discussion points, then Palace are clearly deep into the process.

Matsima also looks like the profile Palace fans tend to warm to, young, talented, athletic and with room to develop further in the Premier League. Supporters always want the club to be brave in the market, and this would qualify as a bold piece of business if it gets done.

There will naturally be some nerves until that “final green light” arrives, because fans have seen plenty of promising deals stall late on. Even so, this feels encouraging. If Palace can get it completed soon, it would send a strong message about the club’s direction and its determination to compete with confidence this season.

title: Sunderland close to complete €30m transfer of Toulouse left-back Dayann Methalie
description: Sunderland are engaged in club-to-club talks with Ligue 1 side Toulouse over the transfer of France U21 international left-back Dayann Methalie (20), according to RMC Sport’s Fabrice Hawkins. The ...
fullText:
Sunderland are engaged in club-to-club talks with Ligue 1 side Toulouse over the transfer of France U21 international left-back Dayann Methalie (20), according to RMC Sport’s Fabrice Hawkins. The Black Cats, who are set to compete in the UEFA Conference League next season, have already secured an agreement on personal terms with Methalie over a five-year contract.

RMC Sport understands that Methalie is valued at around €30m, which would make Methalie the biggest sale of Toulouse’s history. The 20-year-old is billed as one of the best French prospects in the left-back role, with a senior France bow expected in a few years with Lucas Digne and Théo Hernandez entering the twilight of their career.

Club-to-club talks are said to be at an advanced stage between Toulouse and Sunderland. Aston Villa and Newcastle previously enquired about Methalie.

title: Hunter Goodman's poor defense impacts potential Yankees, Red Sox trade
description: Potential trade suitors are concerned with Goodman's catching abilities.
fullText:
Hunter Goodman's poor defense impacts potential Yankees, Red Sox trade originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Hunter Goodman is the top trade candidate from the Colorado Rockies.

Despite the two-time All-Star's 31 home runs and .888 OPS, there is concern around MLB about his defense behind the plate.

Goodman does not grade as a strong defender at catcher. His pop time is below average, and his framing is not strong.

"Yet, interested clubs are resisting the Rockies’ early ask, according to people briefed on the discussions, in part because of their dissatisfaction with Goodman’s work behind the plate," The Athletic's Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon wrote.

Two teams that have a clear need at the catcher's position are the New York Yankees and Boston Red Sox. Will Goodman's struggles with the glove stop their pursuit of the slugger?

"Another exec from a team in need of a catcher said Goodman’s defense was so concerning that his club did not even check with the Rockies about their price," Rosenthal and Sammon added. "Still another said that his club would want a better defensive catcher to part with the prospect capital the Rockies will require."

The Rockies could be in no rush to trade Goodman. He has three years of club control after 2026. Still, this may be a concerning update in the event that the NL West organization decides to seriously consider offers.

"The Rockies, who rank last in the majors in ERA, do not consider Goodman responsible for their pitching woes, according to a person briefed on their thinking," The Athletic duo added. "The bigger issue, they believe, is that their pitchers simply are not good enough."

Goodman's defensive struggles should not fall on the shoulders of Colorado's pitchers, but they could play a part.

Likely, the Rockies' trade requests for Goodman's services will be higher than what teams are willing to accept.

This could lead to the Yankees and Red Sox looking elsewhere for their next upgrade at catcher.

With a routine recovery process, he should be on track to return for Spring Training and offseason programs, though the severity of his injury is still yet to be revealed. Barring unforeseen offseason moves, I'd expect him to garner trade attention once again leading up to the season, and could ultimately be moved before next season's deadline.

title: Darren Till to fight Yoel Romero at BKFC 94
description: Two top contenders from the UFC middleweight division of yesteryear collide this fall.
fullText:
Two former UFC middleweight title challengers will collide without gloves this fall.

Darren Till will have another bareknuckle home game, this time as he headlines BKFC 94 vs. Yoel Romero. The event takes place Sept. 26 at AO Arena in Manchester, England. BKFC president David Feldman announced the matchup Monday on "The Ariel Helwani Show." David Mundell vs. Jack Cullen will serve as the co-main event.

Till (1-0) made his bareknuckle and BKFC debut in May when he defeated former Bellator fighter Aaron Chalmers by second-round TKO. Between his UFC departure in 2023 and his bareknuckle debut, Till went 3-0 in boxing (two exhibitions and one pro bout).

Romero (1-1) has bounced between combat sports disciplines since his PFL departure in 2024, varying from bareknuckle (boxing and MMA), wrestling in RAF, and Dirty Boxing. Romero, 49, debuted in BKFC in September 2025 with a quick finish of Theo Doukas. He competed in bareknuckle in Russia in March, but lost to Vagab Vagabov.

This article originally appeared on MMA Junkie: Darren Till to fight Yoel Romero at BKFC 94

title: 3 Jaguars defenders who need fast starts to training camp
description: These three Jacksonville Jaguars' defenders need to get off to strong starts once training camp practices begin.
fullText:
Every player wants to hit the ground running and start the new season fast once training camp begins. But for which Jacksonville Jaguars players is this a must?

The reasons a strong training camp showing is vital can vary from player to player, but all three of these defensive players require a quick start once practices begin.

For a look at which Jaguars players on offense are under some pressure, you can find that here.

While Josh Hines-Allen and Travon Walker will lead the way at defensive end, this is a heavily rotated position group, with four or five players seeing regular snaps. One of those players expected to fill a key rotational role is rookie Wesley Williams.

Defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile is very bullish on Williams' play style and ability to bring a well-rounded skill set to the defensive front.

His ability to hit the ground running and make a quick impact as a rookie will help determine how disruptive the Jaguars' defensive end unit as a whole can be.

Throughout the offseason, Miller has been the presumed starting linebacker for the Jaguars following Devin Lloyd's departure, and he will enter training camp as the favorite.

However, potentially pushing Miller for those snaps will be Branson Combs. If Miller is unable to get off to a fast start, that will only further open up opportunities for Combs to insert himself and make this a true competition.

Miller had a very strong showing during last summer's training camp, which resulted in him and Lloyd being listed as co-starters on the team's first depth chart. Then, as Lloyd began to take off, he secured that starting role. He'll look to replicate that performance this year.

"I think one of the things he brings to our defense is a physicality in the run game and having been around a few guys like that in the past, I think we got a really good feel for how he fits in and how to use him and really trying to play within his strengths within the defense," Campanile said.

Orhorhoro brings an added pass rush presence to the Jaguars' defensive tackle position. A former second-round pick, Orhorhoro's raw production totals won't jump off the stat sheet. But his role increased last season, and he logged four sacks and 30 quarterback pressures, while ranking 51st out of 121 eligible defensive tackles in PFF's pass rush productivity metric.

A greater pass rush presence from the defensive tackle position is a must for the Jaguars this season. A quick push and steady pressure from the interior defensive line unit is the best way to quickly wreck an offensive play, and when that happens consistently, every defender on the field benefits from it.

Getting more regular pressure on the quarterback from the tackle position will help the defense reach new heights in 2026.

title: Esther González suddenly departs Gotham FC, citing 'personal matters'
description: The forward, a two-time NWSL champion and 2025 MVP finalist, will be returning to Spain in what the club says was a 'mutual contract termination.'
fullText:
Spanish forward and NWSL Golden Boot contender Esther González is departing Gotham FC after mutually terminating her contract, the club announced Monday.

González will "temporarily" step away from soccer to return to her home country of Spain, per the team. Gotham did not include any specifics, saying only that González will "attend to personal matters."

Gracias por todo, Esther 🫶#GothamFC and forward @Estheeer9 have agreed to a mutual contract termination as she temporarily steps away from soccer to attend to personal matters in Spain. We’re wishing her nothing but the best as she takes this time in Spain with her family.… pic.twitter.com/zseWskWA7c

— Gotham FC (@GothamFC) July 27, 2026

González joined the team in 2023, helping lead them to their first NWSL championship. The forward was a finalist for league MVP in 2025, as Gotham once again claimed the championship. González is the club's all-time leading scorer, racking up 30 goals since 2023.

In the team's statement, González said that the club "will always hold a very special place in my heart."

"This journey has surpassed every expectation I had when I first came to Gotham," González said. "Together we achieved everything there is to achieve, and I will forever be proud to say that with this club, I won it all. But beyond the trophies, Gotham is the place where I grew in so many ways — as a player, as a professional and, most importantly, as a person. And it is here, in New Jersey, where my family grew, too."

Born and raised in Huéscar, Spain, González had most recently played for Real Madrid before crossing the pond to join Gotham. González and her wife, Estefanía Cruz, announced in January that they had given birth to their first child.

After a slow start to the season, González had finally started to show flashes. The 33-year-old forward scored two braces in her last three games, knocking in two goals against the Utah Royals on July 10 and against the Seattle Reign on July 18. That brought her up to six goals — short of league scoring leader Barbra Banda, who has 12 goals for the Orlando Pride this year, but moving rapidly up the list.

González was not available for Gotham's 2-2 draw against the Portland Thorns on Friday, with the team citing an excused absence.

González, Gotham's leading scorer this season, will be missed by the team, but her departure does feel timely as the club brings in all-time NWSL leading scorer Sam Kerr. Kerr started in Friday's game with González absent, and scored her first goal since returning to the league.

Pete Lepley, who graduated in 2001, was twice first-team all-state as a football receiver. He had 2,135 yards receiving as a senior, third all-time in the state. Bessie (Artino) Guy, who graduated in 2008, was first-team in the Northern Ohio League for softball four times. She was all-state three times. She hit 27 home runs. She continued her career at Alleghany College and Heidelberg.

Chad Beamer, who graduated in 2002, placed at state in the pole vault four times, including championships as a senior and junior. He was part of two 4x100 relays to finish fifth at state. He rushed for 1,097 yards, including 527 in the football postseason as a senior. He continued his track career at Cincinnati.

Kelli Nasonti, who graduated in 2004, was first-team in the Northern Ohio League for softball as a senior and junior pitcher. She won 30 games those seasons combined. She was first-team all-conference for basketball as a senior. She had 753 points, 558 rebounds and 169 blocks for her career. She played volleyball one year.

Greg Keys, who graduated in 2005, won a track state crown in the 110 hurdles and helped a 4x100 relay finish third as a senior. He qualified to state in 10 events in three seasons, placing eight times. He was second in the 110 hurdles and third in the 300 hurdles as a junior. He was runner-up in both hurdles as a sophomore. He holds the Bellevue record in both hurdles. He was first-team in the Northern Ohio League at running back as a senior. He had 3,137 yards rushing and scored 37 touchdowns in his career. Leslie Raifsnider, who graduated in 2012, finished with the most points in program history at the time at 1,623 for basketball. She held the record for rebounds at 706. Matt Rowland, who graduated in 2013, was first in the state in the pole vault as a senior, junior and sophomore for track. He won the event in the Northern Ohio League four times. He twice was first-team all-state and second-team as a sophomore. He twice rushed for 1,000 yards in a season for football. He continued his baseball career at Morehead State.

Kaitlyn Turinsky, who graduated in 2026, was first-team in the Sandusky Bay Conference Lake Division three times, including player of the year as a senior. She continued her basketball career at Youngstown State.

ESPN is ready to boogie with professional dancing.

The deal with ESPN will see IDL events appear “sporadically” on ESPN2 throughout the season, with other events being available for streaming on ESPN+. The first IDL broadcast on a linear network will be this Tuesday at 7 p.m. ET.

title: Tyleik Williams Reveals Stunning Transformation Before Second Lions Season
description: Tyleik Williams says he lost a massive amount of weight in five months as the Lions defensive tackle prepares for a larger role in his second season.
fullText:
Tyleik Williams entered the NFL known as a powerful interior defender capable of swallowing up blockers and clogging running lanes.

Five months later, the Detroit Lions defensive tackle looks like he may be preparing to become something more.

Williams revealed Monday on social media that he has dropped 50 pounds over the past five months, a dramatic offseason transformation that immediately became one of the biggest Lions storylines heading into training camp. The team still lists him at 325 pounds, though Williams indicated his actual weight had climbed beyond the publicly listed number before he began cutting.

For a player expected to inherit a much larger role in Detroit’s defensive front, the timing could not be better.

Williams spent his rookie season working as part of Detroit’s defensive-line rotation after the Lions selected him No. 28 overall in the 2025 NFL Draft.

He appeared in all 17 games and started 10, finishing with 18 tackles, one sack and four passes defended. Those numbers do not fully capture the job Detroit initially asked him to perform, which centered largely on occupying blockers and holding his ground against the run.

His responsibilities could expand significantly in Year 2.

With veterans DJ Reader and Roy Lopez no longer occupying major snaps inside, Williams enters camp as one of the leading candidates to take on a more prominent role next to Alim McNeill and within Detroit’s defensive-line rotation.

The Lions drafted Williams because of his rare power. A lighter and quicker version could bring a different dimension.

Williams arrived from Ohio State with a reputation as a dependable run defender who still had room to grow as a pass rusher.

That is where the transformation becomes especially interesting.

Dropping excess weight could help Williams improve his first-step quickness, lateral movement and stamina. Rather than being viewed only as a massive early-down defender, he may be able to stay on the field in more passing situations.

Detroit has seen a similar physical change pay off before.

McNeill reshaped his body earlier in his Lions career, reducing body fat and improving his movement without sacrificing the power that made him effective inside. That work helped McNeill develop into a more disruptive pass rusher and a far more complete defensive tackle. Williams’ offseason plan appears to follow a comparable path.

The Lions would gladly take a similar result.

Losing 50 pounds sounds startling for an NFL defensive tackle, but the final number matters less than how Williams performs once the pads come on.

Detroit did not draft him to become a smaller finesse defender.

The Lions still need him to anchor against double teams, control the line of scrimmage and make life easier for Jack Campbell and the rest of the linebackers behind him.

The ideal outcome is not Williams abandoning his power. It is Williams becoming quicker while keeping enough mass and strength to handle the physical demands of the position.

That balance will become one of the first things to watch during camp.

Can he still hold his ground against Detroit’s offensive linemen? Does he move more smoothly during individual drills? Can he generate pressure without relying entirely on strength?

The answers could reshape the Lions’ defensive front.

Aidan Hutchinson remains the player opposing offenses will build their protection plans around.

Detroit cannot ask Hutchinson to create every negative play by himself.

The Lions need pressure from the middle, especially against quarterbacks who are comfortable stepping forward when edge rushers come around the outside. Williams has the frame and strength to collapse that space. Improved conditioning and quickness could help him finish those plays.

That would make Kelvin Sheppard’s defense more difficult to block.

An interior defender who can stop the run and threaten the pocket forces offensive lines into uncomfortable choices. Help inside, and Hutchinson receives more favorable matchups. Focus on Hutchinson, and Williams gets chances to attack one-on-one.

That is the version of Detroit’s defensive line the organization envisioned when it invested a first-round pick in Williams.

Williams will not be judged like a rookie anymore.

He has experienced a complete NFL season, learned what his body must endure and seen exactly where he needs to improve. Losing 50 pounds suggests he did not waste the offseason.

A first-round defensive tackle entering his second year with a clearer path to playing time should become more than a rotational space-eater. Detroit needs Williams to make plays, disrupt protections and become a reliable part of its defensive foundation.

His transformation gives him a chance to do exactly that.

Tyleik Williams did not wait for training camp to make his first major statement of 2026.

The weight loss alone guarantees nothing. Football will provide the real test.

If Williams kept his power while adding speed and endurance, Detroit may be looking at one of the most important breakout candidates on the entire roster.

title: Novak Djokovic-Aryana Sabalenka pairing headline stacked US Open mixed doubles field
description: The US Open introduced a $1 million top prize in 2025 to attract some of the world’s top players to its mixed doubles tournament.  Mission accomplished.
fullText:
The US Open introduced a $1 million top prize in 2025 to attract some of the world’s top players to its mixed doubles tournament.

The second year of the new prize format features a stacked lineup with a pairing of Novak Djokovic and Aryana Sabalenka at the top of the marquee. The US Open announced the pairing Monday as part of the initial list of entrants to the tournament. More are yet to be announced, as are the matchups.

Djokovic is a 24-time Grand Slam champion and four-time singles winner at the US Open. Sabalenka is the world No. 1, a four-time Grand Slam winner and the two-time reigning US Open champion in singles. They’ll be joined be other high-profiles singles players in the mixed doubles draw.

Six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Świątek will join Casper Ruud again after the pairing advanced to the final of last year’s mixed doubles tournament. Other standout pairings include Jessica Pegula and Jack Draper, Elena Rybakina and Taylor Fritz, Leylah Fernandez and Frances Tiafoe and Naomi Osaka and Kei Nishikori.

Mixed doubles specialists Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori will also return in search of their third consecutive US Open title. The new format drew criticism last year for prioritizing big-name singles players over traditional mixed doubles specialists like Errani and Vavassori. But Errani and Vavassori prevailed over the field and defeated Świątek and Ruud in the final to capture the third of their four mixed doubles Grand Slam titles.

Mixed doubles play is scheduled to start on Aug 24, and the final is scheduled for Aug 26. The first round of the US Open singles draw is scheduled to start on Aug. 30.

title: Cracker Barrel CEO steps down a year after logo debacle
description: Cracker Barrel's CEO is stepping down nearly a year after an attempted rebrand of the chain led to a fierce customer backlash.  Cracker Barrel said Monday that CEO Julie Masino will step down next month but remain with the company until Oct. 9 in an advisory capacity.  David Deno will succeed Masino on Aug. 10 as CEO.
fullText:
Cracker Barrel's CEO is stepping down nearly a year after an attempted rebrand of the chain led to a fierce customer backlash.

Cracker Barrel said Monday that CEO Julie Masino will step down next month but remain with the company until Oct. 9 in an advisory capacity.

David Deno will succeed Masino on Aug. 10 as CEO. Deno served as the CEO of Bloomin' Brands, which owns Outback Steakhouse and other chains, from 2019 until he retired in 2024. He has also held executive roles as Best Buy and Yum Brands, which is the parent company of KFC and Taco Bell.

Lebanon, Tennessee-based Cracker Barrel hired Masino, a longtime Taco Bell and Starbucks executive, in July 2023. She was chosen for her record as an innovator with the hope that she would attract new customers to Cracker Barrel, which operates nearly 660 restaurants in 43 states.

Masino introduced updated menu items, like Hashbrown Casserole Shepherd's Pie, to increase Cracker Barrel's dinnertime traffic. She also started remodeling the company's dark, antique-filled restaurants, lightening the walls and installing more comfortable seating.

Then, last August, Cracker Barrel announced plans to ditch its longtime logo, which features an older, overall-clad man leaning on a barrel as well as the words "Old Country Store." The company said it would continue to honor Uncle Herschel — the man in its logo, who represents the uncle of Cracker Barrel's founder — on its menu and on items sold in its stores. But the new logo would be simpler and easier to read on road signs and in phone apps.

The backlash was immediate. Fans didn't like the new logo and also rebelled against the store redesigns. Even President Donald Trump weighed in, saying in a Truth Social post that Cracker Barrel "should go back to the old logo, admit a mistake based on customer response (the ultimate Poll), and manage the company better than ever before."

Masino reversed course within a few days, but the damage was done. Cracker Barrel's same-store restaurant sales plunged 5% last fall and 7% in the quarter ending Jan. 30, 2026. Same-store sales at the retail stores connected to its restaurants dropped even further.

Still, the company's shareholders voted in November to keep Masino in place as CEO, and sales trends had begun to improve in recent months. In the quarter ending May 1, same-store restaurant sales were down 2.6% and the company raised its full-year revenue and profit forecast.

Masino also helped sharpen the company's focus on the Cracker Barrel brand with the sale of the company's Maple Street Biscuit Co. stores. Cracker Barrel acquired Maple Street in 2019 and operated 50 locations around the country.

Citi analyst Jon Tower said in a research note Monday that the news of Masino's departure was surprising given those recent improvements.

Cracker Barrel shares fell 2.7% in early afternoon trading.

title: 3 dead, 4 injured after shooting at Seattle food festival
description: The Seattle Police Department is investigating a shooting that left multiple people injured at the Seattle Center on Sunday, July 26.
fullText:
Editor's note: This page summarizes news of the Seattle shooting on Sunday, July 26. For the latest on the Seattle Center shooting, visit USA TODAY's coverage for Monday, July 27.

Police in Seattle are investigating a mass shooting near the city's iconic Space Needle on July 26 that left three people dead and four others injured, including a toddler.

Officers took a suspect into custody following the early evening shooting, Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson said in an updated statement. The mayor previously said two people were in custody.

A second individual was also believed to be involved, and officers were searching for that person, Seattle Police Department Assistant Chief Tyrone Davis said in a media briefing late on Sunday.

The shooting took place at the Seattle Center, a 74-acre entertainment and cultural complex just northwest of downtown Seattle, that hosted the Bite of Seattle food festival this weekend.

Founded in 1982, Bite of Seattle has been a summer tradition in the Northwest for over 40 years and featured over 130 food and beverage vendors, along with live cooking demos, live music and other activities.

"What happened at the Seattle Center today was an act of horrific violence," Wilson said. "Impacted families are living through the worst moment of their lives, and an entire community is trying to understand how a gathering built around culture, connection, and joy ended in gunfire. No one should have to weigh the risk of being shot before attending an event, gathering with friends, or experiencing their city."

The Seattle Fire Department told USA TODAY the shooting took place about 6 p.m. PT and, despite lifesaving efforts, two people were pronounced dead at the scene.

Four others were taken to a hospital, firefighters said, and another person who suffered minor injuries, a 40-year-old woman, declined to be transported for medical treatment.

Davis said one person in hospital died of their injuries, bringing the death toll to three. He added that the four others in hospital were in stable condition.

The other victims include a 56-year-old woman, a 39-year-old woman, a 23-year-old man, and a 2-year-old boy. It was not immediately known which of the victims taken to a hospital died.

USA TODAY reached out to police 

"We know that many people who were not physically injured will carry what they experienced today for a long time," Wilson said. "That includes witnesses, workers, first responders, and everyone waiting to learn whether someone they love is safe."

'Cannot accept this violence as normal': Man charged after fatal shooting of 12-year-old outside NYC bodega

Estan Wakonabo, 35, told The Seattle Times he was at Bite of Seattle with his girlfriend when the gunshots rang out.

"It was just pure chaos," Wakonabo said, telling the outlet he watched people trample over one another during the melee and later saw several gunshot victims on the ground.

Later in the evening, in a post on X, Gov. Bob Ferguson wrote the Washington State Patrol SWAT team was on the way to assist, at the request of Seattle police.

"My prayers are with the families of the victims, and the responders as they work to keep people safe," Ferguson wrote.

U.S. Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Washington, in a post on X, called the shooting "senseless violence" and said local and state leaders, including Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson and Ferguson, were continuing to monitor the fluid situation.

"We are grateful to law enforcement at SPD and first responders who are at the scene and working hard," Jayapal wrote. "Our hearts go out to all those impacted by this senseless violence. We will provide updates as we have additional information."

Multiple other local, state and federal agencies, including the FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, also responded to the scene.

"Gun violence changes families forever. Its trauma reaches far beyond the people struck by bullets. In the days ahead, we will establish what happened and be transparent with the public about what we have learned," Wilson said. "Tonight, our attention belongs to the people whose lives were taken, those fighting to recover, and the families beside them."

"Seattle grieves with you, and we will stand with you in the difficult days ahead," she said.

Contributing: Zachary Fletcher with the Kitsap Sun, part of the USA TODAY Network, Reuters

Natalie Neysa Alund is a senior reporter for USA TODAY. Reach her at nalund@usatoday.com and follow her on X @nataliealund.
